alt: Section B is 45 marks for one task chosen from two prompts: 27 for AO4 (adapting form, tone and register for purpose and audience) and 18 for AO5 (vocabulary, sentences and accuracy). It has about 45 minutes, after Section A, in a 2 hour 15 minute paper.
caption: AO4 is 27 marks, but AO5 counts in every sentence.

after: ## Reading the prompt: purpose, audience, form
alt: One issue, school food, written two ways: a speech to classmates can be lively and direct, while a letter to a council needs a formal, courteous tone. Purpose, audience and form together decide the register.
caption: Purpose, audience and form decide the register.

after: ## The six forms and their conventions
alt: Six cards, one per form: article, speech, letter, guide, review and text of a leaflet. Each lists the conventions examiners expect, such as a headline for an article, signposting for a speech and a requested action at the end of a letter, with a register note in teal.
caption: Use each form’s conventions, but only in service of the purpose.

alt: A plan for a persuasive speech to Year 10 students: an opening scene or question, two reasons with an example and a contrast, a counter-argument answered, what the audience can do, and a close that returns to the opening image. The ending is planned before writing begins.
caption: Five to seven points, with the ending decided first.

alt: Three parts of the litter-picking speech opening, each annotated: the greeting and “Look at your shoes” create a spoken, inclusive voice; “I did too” admits shared guilt and persuades without lecturing; the last sentence signposts the argument and sets a request. A short imperative, a long cumulative sentence and a three-word sentence give deliberate variety.
caption: Each sentence of the opening does a job for audience, purpose or structure.

alt: Five AO5 habits: vary sentence lengths deliberately, choose precise rather than inflated vocabulary (“neglected” rather than “very bad”), paragraph for each new point, use colons, semicolons and dashes for their jobs, and keep three minutes to proofread for missing words, comma splices and homophones.
caption: Precise, accurate and deliberate beats long and showy.
